question: A clinical preceptor washes their hands before every room entry, and soon the students do the same naturally. What theory explains this?

options.A: Behaviorist punishment theory
options.B: Andragogical adult testing
options.C: Social learning theory
options.D: Humanistic hierarchy theory

explanation: Exactly! The students watched a trusted role model practice good habits and naturally picked up the same great routine.

question: A patient has a stroke affecting the left frontal lobe. As a nurse, what sign might you notice?

options.A: Total loss of hearing in both ears
options.B: Complete blindness in the left eye
options.C: Difficulty with voluntary movement on the right side
options.D: Inability to recognize familiar faces

explanation: The frontal lobe handles movement. Because brain pathways cross over, the left side of your brain controls the right side of your body!

question: What is the main job of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)?

options.A: It breaks down stored fat to generate body heat and energy.
options.B: It prevents the hypothalamus from releasing thyrotropin-releasing hormone.
options.C: It signals the thyroid gland to produce and release thyroid hormones.
options.D: It directly lowers high blood calcium levels in the bloodstream.

explanation: You got it! TSH is released by the pituitary gland to tell the thyroid when it's time to make and pump out more hormones.

question: What is the main issue in retrograde ejaculation?

options.A: Sperm cells fail to mature inside the epididymis
options.B: The testes produce zero fluid during the emission phase
options.C: Skeletal muscles contract too slowly to move semen
options.D: Semen flows backward into the urinary bladder

explanation: Spot on! When the bladder neck muscle fails to close properly, semen goes backward into the bladder instead of out.

question: A 10-month-old cannot sit unsupported, keeps fists clenched, and has stiff legs that cross like scissors when lifted. What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal infant development
options.B: A mild viral ear infection
options.C: Cerebral palsy
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Delayed sitting, tight fists, and scissoring legs are classic signs that point towards cerebral palsy during developmental checks.

question: What happens immediately to your body when stress hormones like adrenaline rush into your bloodstream?

options.A: Digestion speeds up and saliva increases
options.B: Blood vessels in the muscles constrict
options.C: Heart rate and blood pressure increase
options.D: Pupils constrict to focus on close objects

explanation: Adrenaline gets you ready for action! Your heart pumps faster, blood pressure goes up, and your body preps you to run or fight. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h2)

question: Why should nurses mix professional standards into the daily nursing process?

options.A: It stops patients from asking questions about treatment
options.B: It shortens the length of a nurse's working shift
options.C: It eliminates the need to document patient care
options.D: It ensures care is safe, consistent, and evidence-based

explanation: Using professional standards as you work guarantees that every single patient gets top-quality, proven care they can trust.

question: Why must a scrub nurse know the exact name and purpose of every surgical instrument?

options.A: It is a legal requirement for writing the patient's record
options.B: It helps the doctor finish the operation without speaking
options.C: It prevents prolonged surgery and accidental tissue damage
options.D: It stops the instruments from rusting during the procedure

explanation: Knowing your tools allows you to anticipate the surgeon's needs quickly, keeping the operation safe and efficient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h1)

question: A patient has an infected wound on their right hand and notices tender lumps in their right armpit. What does this mean?

options.A: The patient has a primary blood disorder originating in the spleen
options.B: The patient is experiencing normal side effects of red blood cell breakdown
options.C: Bacteria from the hand wound are traveling through lymph vessels to the axillary nodes
options.D: Blockage of the thoracic duct has caused fluid backup in the upper extremity

explanation: Lymph drains from specific regions of the body to nearby nodes. An infection in the hand travels up the arm vessels, causing the armpit (axillary) nodes to trap the germs and swell up.

question: What usually happens to the price of a medical service when demand for it rises significantly?

options.A: The price increases
options.B: The price remains strictly fixed by law
options.C: The price drops to zero
options.D: The price becomes irrelevant

explanation: Higher demand for a limited service naturally drives prices upward in a free market environment. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h2)

question: How do good communication skills help families stay healthy?

options.A: They dictate strict financial rules for family members
options.B: They reduce conflict and help members express needs clearly
options.C: They ensure that arguments never happen in any household
options.D: They replace the need for physical health checkups

explanation: When family members talk openly and listen well, they solve problems faster and keep peace in the home.

question: What is the name of the medication commonly used to treat an unruptured ectopic pregnancy medically?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Methotrexate

explanation: Methotrexate is a chemotherapy drug that stops rapid cell division, safely ending an early ectopic pregnancy without surgery. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T29#GNS216_U5_T29_h6)

question: Why do healthcare workers often suggest taking citrus fruits or tomatoes along with iron-rich foods?

options.A: Citrus fruits stop the common side effect of constipation
options.B: It prevents the iron supplement from dissolving too fast
options.C: Acidic foods completely remove the metallic taste of iron
options.D: Vitamin C helps the body absorb iron much better

explanation: Vitamin C acts like a friendly helper—it teams up with iron so your tummy can absorb it easily and keep your blood strong!

question: What should you do with a surgical instrument that has a broken ratchet during inspection?

options.A: Removed from circulation immediately
options.B: Stored in the sterile room for minor procedures
options.C: Sent straight to the sterilization autoclave
options.D: Wrapped tightly in a double linen layer

explanation: You got it! Damaged tools won't work right during surgery and tiny cracks can hide bacteria. Pull them out of use right away.

question: Which of the following describes a standing plan in nursing?

options.A: A sudden emergency order that is never used again
options.B: A standardized guideline used repeatedly for recurring situations
options.C: A one-time budget created for a hospital building project
options.D: A five-year goal set by the board of directors

explanation: Standing plans like hospital policies and standard operating procedures are designed to be used over and over for routine situations. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h5)

question: What does drug non-compliance mean in nursing practice?

options.A: A doctor writing an illegible prescription slip
options.B: A nurse administering the wrong dose of medication
options.C: A pharmacy running out of essential prescribed drugs
options.D: A patient failing to follow a prescribed medication regimen

explanation: Non-compliance simply means the patient is not taking their drugs the way the doctor or nurse instructed them to. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h1)

question: You are posted to a rural village where women have closely spaced pregnancies. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise community leaders to ban all marriages for young women
options.B: Wait for patients to visit the hospital before discussing reproductive health
options.C: Organize community education on birth spacing and offer family planning counseling
options.D: Focus all clinic resources exclusively on geriatric care programs

explanation: Fantastic! Taking education directly to the community helps families learn about safe birth spacing and maternal health.

question: A community health nurse notices a 12-year-old girl has suddenly stopped coming to school and clinic. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Ignore the absence since it falls outside routine clinical nursing duties
options.B: Investigate the reason for absence through a home visit or family talk
options.C: Report the family to the international criminal court immediately
options.D: Wait until the end of the year to see if the child returns on her own

explanation: That's right! A sudden dropout is a red flag. Checking in with the family helps you find out what's going on and offer support early.

question: Which action is critical for breaking the chain of transmission during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: Waiting patiently for the disease to run its course naturally
options.B: Focusing solely on hospital administrative paperwork
options.C: Isolating infectious individuals and tracing their contacts
options.D: Stopping all routine cleaning supplies distribution

explanation: Great job! Finding who was exposed and keeping sick people away from healthy people is how you successfully halt an infection's spread.

question: A patient takes 15 seconds to complete the Timed Up and Go test. How should the nurse interpret this result?

options.A: The patient has normal mobility for an adult
options.B: The patient needs immediate cardiac monitoring
options.C: The patient has a high risk for falls
options.D: The patient requires upper limb strength training

explanation: A completion time exceeding 12 seconds on the TUG test is a standard indicator that an older adult is at an increased risk of falling. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T5#GNS324_U6_T5_h2)

question: In simple terms, what does cellular hypoxia mean for the body's tissues?

options.A: An excess of sugar circulating in the blood
options.B: A dangerous shortage of oxygen supply
options.C: A sudden increase in total body water volume
options.D: A high concentration of red blood cells

explanation: Hypo means low, and oxia refers to oxygen. It simply means the cells are crying out for the oxygen they need to work!

question: What is the primary goal of health care financing in a population?

options.A: Mobilizing, pooling, and allocating funds for health services
options.B: Generating high profits for pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Eliminating private hospitals from the healthcare market
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing training institutions

explanation: Health financing is fundamentally about gathering and distributing money to pay for needed health services. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h1)

question: How is segmentation different from peristalsis in the digestive tract?

options.A: Segmentation occurs only in the stomach, while peristalsis happens in the colon.
options.B: Segmentation relies on skeletal muscle, while peristalsis uses smooth muscle.
options.C: Segmentation stops digestion, while peristalsis speeds up absorption.
options.D: Segmentation mixes food back and forth, while peristalsis pushes food forward.

explanation: Think of peristalsis as a wave pushing food down a slide, while segmentation is more like stirring soup back and forth to mix it thoroughly with digestive juices!

question: Which serious side effect should nurses watch out for in patients taking fertility drugs for IVF ovarian stimulation?

options.A: Sudden permanent hair loss
options.B: Chronic iron-deficiency anemia
options.C: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome
options.D: Complete cessation of urine output from kidney failure

explanation: Brilliant! OHSS happens when ovaries swell up and leak fluid, and a sharp nurse spots this early. You're thinking like a pro!

question: What does alignment mean within the hierarchy of objectives?

options.A: Doctors and nurses must share the same university degree
options.B: All nurses must work the exact same number of day and night shifts
options.C: Every department must have the exact same financial budget
options.D: Lower-level goals directly support and connect to upper-level goals

explanation: Alignment ensures that operational, tactical, and strategic goals work together without contradiction. [learn more](GST321_U2_T3#GST321_U2_T3_h6)

question: How do illegal buildings put over drainage channels affect urban flooding?

options.A: They improve the response time of ambulances during storms
options.B: They worsen urban flooding by blocking the natural flow of water
options.C: They provide safe temporary shelters for displaced families
options.D: They serve as command centers for emergency rescue teams

explanation: When waterways are blocked by construction, rainwater has nowhere to go, causing heavy and destructive floods in the city. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is a major operational challenge to routine immunization coverage in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of refrigeration units in primary clinics
options.B: Geographic barriers and hard-to-reach rural settlements
options.C: Too many trained nurses available for community outreach
options.D: A complete absence of infectious diseases in the country

explanation: Getting vaccines across rivers, bad roads, and remote terrain to reach every single child is one of our biggest field challenges.

question: A village has issues with both scabies and severe malaria. The nurse prioritizes malaria because it kills many young children. What guiding principle is this?

options.A: Ease of writing survey forms
options.B: Total number of adult males employed
options.C: Availability of foreign travel grants
options.D: Severity and urgency

explanation: Spot on! When a condition is life-threatening, its severity and urgency push it straight to the top of your priority list.

question: Why do nurses and researchers use a scatter diagram?

options.A: To track a single patient's temperature over time
options.B: To calculate the exact medication dosage for a child
options.C: To compare infection rates across four different states
options.D: To explore the relationship between two variables

explanation: Scatter diagrams help us see if two different factors are connected or related to each other visually. Great job!

question: What is the main goal of food fortification programs in public health?

options.A: Removing harmful chemical additives from local markets
options.B: Extending the shelf life of perishable meats
options.C: Adding essential nutrients to everyday foods to protect populations
options.D: Lowering the market cost of imported luxury foods

explanation: You got it! Fortifying common foods like salt or flour ensures that whole communities get key nutrients like iron and iodine without changing their daily habits.

question: What historic international conference officially launched the global primary health care movement in 1978?

options.A: The Abuja Health Summit
options.B: The Geneva Nursing Accord
options.C: The Lagos Charter on Health
options.D: The Alma-Ata Declaration

explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration in 1978 set the foundation for global primary health care and the goal of Health for All. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)

question: How does community stigma negatively affect disease surveillance efforts?

options.A: It encourages patients to report early to tertiary medical centers
options.B: It improves the accuracy of hospital laboratory diagnostic registers
options.C: It forces public health officers to increase local vaccination budgets
options.D: It causes families to hide sick members, leading to missed cases and deaths

explanation: Spot on! When people are afraid of being stigmatized, they hide their sick loved ones, making it tough for health workers to track and stop outbreaks.

question: Why do standard antibiotics fail to cure viral infections like the common cold?

options.A: Antibiotics are destroyed by stomach acid before reaching viral cells
options.B: Viruses mutate too quickly for white blood cells to recognize them
options.C: Viruses hide inside healthy red blood cells away from medicines
options.D: Viruses do not possess the cellular structures that antibiotics target

explanation: Remember, antibiotics attack bacterial walls or parts that viruses simply don't have. That's why taking antibiotics for a viral flu won't help!

question: Why do nurses champion routine immunization as a powerful tool in public health?

options.A: It transforms harmful chemical agents into harmless substances
options.B: It instantly cures patients who are already showing active symptoms
options.C: It completely destroys all environmental reservoirs of the pathogen
options.D: It makes potential hosts immune before they ever encounter the agent

explanation: Vaccines train the body's immune system ahead of time so it's ready to block the germ the very second it tries to enter!

question: What is the very first step when planning a nursing audit?

options.A: Buying new computers for the nursing office
options.B: Establishing criteria and standards of care
options.C: Punishing nurses who fail to write reports
options.D: Discharging all patients from the medical ward

explanation: Makes total sense! We have to decide what excellent care looks like first before we can measure our actual work against it.

question: What usually happens when a healthcare facility does not have a clear organisational structure?

options.A: Better coordination among different hospital departments
options.B: Instant improvement in employee satisfaction scores
options.C: Confusion over job roles and delayed decisions
options.D: A sharp increase in the recruitment of new nurses

explanation: Without clear reporting lines, staff get confused about whose job is whose, and simple decisions take forever. A clear structure prevents this headache!

question: Where is the safest place to throw away a used injection needle immediately after giving an injection?

options.A: In an open cardboard box on the desk
options.B: In the general sink drain for washing
options.C: In a regular black plastic trash bag
options.D: In a puncture-proof safety box

explanation: Well done! Sharps boxes protect you and your colleagues from accidental needle-prick injuries.

question: Which of these clinical situations is a classic reason to order an EPS?

options.A: Unexplained fainting spells
options.B: Newly diagnosed mild anemia
options.C: Chronic lower back pain
options.D: Suspected acute bronchitis

explanation: When a patient keeps fainting and nobody knows why, doctors use an EPS to check if a sudden dangerous heart rhythm is the sneaky culprit.

question: Your clinical tutor watches you clean a wound, points out a mistake, and shows you the right way right there. What kind of evaluation is this?

options.A: Norm-referenced
options.B: Formative
options.C: Financial
options.D: Summative

explanation: Spot-on! Catching a mistake and correcting it on the spot to help you learn is a classic formative assessment.

question: What is a major benefit of a junior nurse being mentored by an experienced researcher?

options.A: It allows the junior nurse to escape night shift duties permanently
options.B: It provides mentorship that demystifies publication and data analysis
options.C: It fulfills the legal requirement for hospital budget approval
options.D: It guarantees immediate international grants for the hospital

explanation: Mentorship is a game-changer! Having an experienced guide takes the fear out of research and shows you that publishing is totally doable.

question: What term describes the grief family members feel while watching a loved one slowly decline before death occurs?

options.A: Complicated grief
options.B: Anticipatory grief
options.C: Pathological mourning
options.D: Delayed bereavement

explanation: Anticipatory grief happens before a death actually occurs, as families process the impending loss during a prolonged illness. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h4)

question: A patient with severe malnutrition is admitted to your ward. Why are they at high risk for opportunistic infections?

options.A: Poor nutrition compromises their immune defenses and breaks down physical barriers
options.B: Lack of nutrients stops medications from working inside the bloodstream
options.C: Their body temperature permanently rises to a level that fosters bacterial growth
options.D: Malnourished tissues attract higher concentrations of ambient airborne viruses

explanation: Good clinical thinking! Without proper food and nutrients, the body cannot build strong immune cells or maintain tough physical barriers like skin and mucous membranes.

question: Around which week of pregnancy do hCG levels usually hit their highest peak?

options.A: Around the tenth week
options.B: Right after delivery of the placenta
options.C: At the moment of fertilization
options.D: Just before active labor begins

explanation: That's right! hCG shoots up super fast in the early weeks and peaks right around week ten before starting to drop down.

question: When is it safe to have unprotected sex using the basal body temperature method without risking pregnancy?

options.A: Throughout the entire first week of the menstrual cycle
options.B: During the morning when the temperature spike is first noticed
options.C: On the exact day the temperature drops to its lowest point
options.D: After the temperature has remained elevated for three consecutive mornings

explanation: Three days of higher temperatures confirm that ovulation has already happened and the egg is gone. Safe zone unlocked!

question: A young woman presents to the clinic months after a traditional birth procedure complaining of continuous urine leakage and severe social isolation. What condition should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Stress incontinence
options.B: Urinary tract infection
options.C: Kidney stones
options.D: Vesicovaginal fistula

explanation: Continuous, uncontrollable leaking of urine following traditional vaginal cutting is the classic presentation of a vesicovaginal fistula. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T16#GNS312_U1_T16_h4)

question: Why do doctors send the tissue from a removed cervical polyp to the lab?

options.A: To measure hormone receptor levels
options.B: To determine the patient's blood type
options.C: To confirm it is benign and rule out cancer
options.D: To check for viral resistance to antibiotics

explanation: Sending it to the lab is just a routine way to double-check under a microscope that everything is truly non-cancerous.

question: How do large conferences usually differ from smaller seminars in nursing education?

options.A: Seminars always last for an entire week while conferences last only one hour.
options.B: Seminars focus exclusively on international health policies rather than clinical work.
options.C: Conferences are larger gatherings covering broad trends and offering networking opportunities.
options.D: Conferences are strictly hands-on practical sessions held in small hospital rooms.

explanation: Think of a conference as a big gathering where nurses from all over meet to share big ideas and research, while seminars are smaller, cozy deep-dives into specific topics.

question: When is radiation therapy usually added to a patient's treatment plan for vulval tumours?

options.A: Only to prevent normal hair from growing back on the labia
options.B: As the absolute first choice for tiny benign cysts
options.C: To replace the need for any diagnostic skin biopsies
options.D: For advanced cases or when surgery is not a safe option

explanation: Correct! Radiation is typically used when the cancer has spread too far for simple surgery, or if the patient's health makes surgery too risky.

question: A nurse teaches primary school pupils about handwashing. Six weeks later, she checks if the rate of diarrhea among the children has dropped. What type of evaluation is this?

options.A: Financial budgeting
options.B: Impact evaluation
options.C: Logistical planning
options.D: Baseline assessment

explanation: Spot on! Looking at long-term health changes—like a drop in illness rates—tells you the real impact your teaching made.

question: Which of these is a major challenge to quality assurance in many Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: Shortages of nursing personnel and equipment
options.B: Excessive funding for nursing research programs
options.C: Too many nurses working in rural health centers
options.D: An overabundance of advanced medical technology

explanation: Unfortunately, staff shortages and a lack of basic tools are very real hurdles we face when trying to maintain high care standards in many of our hospitals.

question: Why do some sleeping pills sometimes fail to give patients truly refreshing rest?

options.A: They permanently damage the brainstem respiratory control centers
options.B: They cause severe dehydration and electrolyte imbalance during sleep
options.C: They distort normal sleep stages by suppressing deep and rapid eye movement sleep
options.D: They cause the patient to sleep for less than two hours per night

explanation: Certain sleeping pills mess with your natural sleep cycle, blocking you from getting enough of that crucial deep sleep and REM rest.

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard piece of guidance a nurse should give to promote healthy circulation in a pregnant woman?

options.A: Avoid standing motionless in one spot for long periods of time
options.B: Change positions slowly when getting up from a chair or bed
options.C: Sleep on your side to prevent compression of major blood vessels
options.D: Lie completely flat on your back whenever resting during the day

explanation: Lying flat on the back compresses the vena cava and drops cardiac output, so side-lying positions are strongly preferred. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h6)

question: What is the main reason teenagers often avoid seeking healthcare for sensitive personal issues?

options.A: Preference for traditional herbal remedies only
options.B: Fear of parents or community members finding out
options.C: A lack of interest in personal hygiene
options.D: The high cost of prescription eyeglasses

explanation: Without guaranteed privacy, teens worry about gossip and judgment from adults they know in the community. Privacy builds trust!

question: If a patient catches a really strong (virulent) strain of bacteria, what are they most likely to experience?

options.A: A much longer and milder incubation window
options.B: Zero replication inside the lymphatic system
options.C: Complete immunity without ever showing symptoms
options.D: A shorter incubation period with faster symptom onset

explanation: You got it! Highly virulent bugs cause tissue damage rapidly, meaning symptoms pop up much faster.

question: Which tier of government in Nigeria has the primary responsibility for running grassroots primary healthcare?

options.A: Federal Government only
options.B: Traditional royal palaces
options.C: Local Government Areas
options.D: Private international donors

explanation: Local Government Areas (LGAs) are tasked with the daily grassroots delivery of PHC to our towns and villages.

question: Why is it best to look for local strengths in the community before asking for outside donations?

options.A: External organizations refuse to work with community nurses
options.B: Local materials are always completely free of charge
options.C: Outside donors are legally banned from helping health clinics
options.D: It builds self-reliance so the program can keep running long-term

explanation: Spot on! Using local assets empowers the community so the project doesn't collapse the moment outside help stops.

question: What is the best way to start counselling a mother whose child is experiencing growth faltering?

options.A: Tell the mother to stop coming to the clinic until next year
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about recent feeding and illness
options.C: Scold the mother for failing to feed the child properly
options.D: Write a prescription for expensive imported vitamin supplements

explanation: Great nursing starts with empathy and listening. Ask gentle, open questions to understand what's happening at home without judging.

question: A patient with sickle cell anaemia suddenly complains of a severe headache and trouble speaking. What is your priority nursing action?

options.A: Administer a mild oral pain reliever and reassess the patient in one hour
options.B: Perform a prompt neurological assessment and notify the primary provider immediately
options.C: Encourage the patient to drink two large glasses of cold water right away
options.D: Apply a warm compress to the forehead and turn off the overhead room lights

explanation: Trust your nursing instincts! Sudden neurological changes in a sickle cell patient can mean a stroke is happening. This is a medical emergency that needs immediate action.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the three social needs in McClelland's theory?

options.A: Need for achievement
options.B: Need for biological survival
options.C: Need for affiliation
options.D: Need for power

explanation: Spot on! McClelland focuses on learned social needs (achievement, affiliation, and power), not basic biological survival.

question: How does the ongoing brain drain impact the nurses who decide to stay and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: They automatically receive double salaries from government funds
options.B: They are barred from attending professional nursing conferences
options.C: They must close down all public primary health centers
options.D: They face heavier workloads, burnout, and dangerous nurse-to-patient ratios

explanation: That's right. When colleagues leave, the remaining nurses have to pick up the slack, leading to severe exhaustion and stretched resources.

question: Why do different organizational cultures, such as military versus humanitarian groups, cause friction in a response?

options.A: They operate under conflicting leadership styles and operational rules
options.B: Humanitarian workers refuse to wear protective boots
options.C: They are legally forbidden from speaking to one another in public
options.D: They always use completely different spoken languages

explanation: Rigid military hierarchies and flexible volunteer groups often clash over how decisions should be made in the field. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T7#GNS315_U5_T7_h7)

question: Why does the amygdala let you react to danger before you even have time to think?

options.A: Danger signals reach the amygdala super fast before slow conscious thought kicks in
options.B: Rational thought happens only inside the spinal cord
options.C: The cerebral cortex controls all immediate physical reflexes
options.D: The amygdala temporarily shuts down the eyes to focus on hearing

explanation: Exactly! Messages from your senses take a fast track to the amygdala so you can react quickly to danger before your thinking brain even catches up.

question: Why can an untreated lower vaginal infection lead to problems with getting pregnant?

options.A: Infections can travel upward through the uterus and scar the fallopian tubes
options.B: Bacterial toxins permanently stop the pituitary gland from releasing hormones
options.C: Inflammation completely closes the outer vaginal opening with scar tissue
options.D: Microbes directly destroy all developing eggs stored inside the ovaries

explanation: Spot on! Infections can move up (like in pelvic inflammatory disease) and leave scars that block the tubes, making it hard for eggs to travel.

question: What kind of workplace environment do nurses need so they feel safe reporting when a test goes wrong?

options.A: Mandatory overtime pay
options.B: Advanced computer coding skills
options.C: Psychological safety
options.D: Strict punitive measures

explanation: Psychological safety means you can speak up honestly about mistakes or failed trials without fear of being yelled at or punished. Every good nursing team needs this!

question: How does a pregnant woman's total blood volume usually change during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It decreases sharply to prevent high blood pressure.
options.B: It remains completely unchanged throughout gestation.
options.C: It increases by nearly half to support the placenta.
options.D: It fluctuates wildly based on daily fluid intake.

explanation: Amazing body fact: a mum's blood volume expands by almost 50% to make sure the baby and placenta get all the blood and oxygen they need!

question: How does severe financial stress usually affect a patient managing a physical disability?

options.A: It ends their need for community support
options.B: It causes immediate bone degeneration
options.C: It makes them less likely to follow their prescribed care plan
options.D: It automatically cures their chronic condition

explanation: When money is tight, patients often have to choose between feeding their families and buying meds or attending follow-up clinics. Financial stress makes adherence very difficult!

question: A nurse accidentally drops and breaks an old mercury blood pressure machine on the ward floor. What kind of hazard is this?

options.A: Chemical hazard
options.B: Biological hazard
options.C: Genotoxic hazard
options.D: Radioactive hazard

explanation: Mercury is a toxic heavy metal, making it a chemical hazard. Its vapors can easily be breathed in or absorbed through the skin if not cleaned up properly!

question: What is the main focus of emergency nursing?

options.A: Providing long-term physical rehabilitation
options.B: Managing chronic lifestyle diseases at home
options.C: Conducting routine annual health screenings
options.D: Saving lives and stabilizing sudden illnesses

explanation: Emergency nurses specialize in immediate, acute interventions to stabilize patients facing life-threatening situations. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h1)

question: During a home visit, a patient with severe anxiety mentions thoughts of ending their life. What is the nurse's priority action?

options.A: Tell the patient to snap out of it and focus on positive thoughts
options.B: Wait until the next scheduled clinic appointment in two weeks
options.C: Advise the patient to exercise vigorously until exhausted
options.D: Assess the immediate suicide risk and ensure a safe environment

explanation: You nailed it. Safety always comes first. When a patient talks about self-harm, assessing immediate risk is the most crucial step.

question: What is the main difference between normal, everyday worry and a true anxiety disorder?

options.A: Anxiety disorders have no physical symptoms, unlike normal stress.
options.B: Normal anxiety only occurs in children, while anxiety disorders only affect adults.
options.C: Normal anxiety requires prescription medication to resolve.
options.D: Normal anxiety fades after the threat passes, while an anxiety disorder is chronic and disrupts daily life.

explanation: You've got this! Normal worry comes and goes with life's stresses. An anxiety disorder sticks around, making everyday tasks really tough. Spotting this difference helps us know when a patient needs extra support.

question: Why is the psychological trauma of breast ironing often exceptionally severe for young girls?

options.A: It is openly discussed by the entire community every day
options.B: It is inflicted by trusted family members meant to protect them
options.C: It forces victims to drop out of school permanently
options.D: It causes immediate and total memory loss

explanation: When mothers or grandmothers commit the abuse, the child experiences a severe betrayal of trust. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h5)

question: Why should you avoid checking blood pressure on the arm of a patient who has had lymph nodes removed from that side?

options.A: It causes immediate permanent damage to the brachial artery
options.B: It can impair fluid drainage and trigger severe lymphedema
options.C: The blood pressure reading will always read falsely high
options.D: It stops white blood cells from maturing in the bone marrow

explanation: When lymph nodes are removed, drainage in that limb is already fragile. Squeezing the arm with a blood pressure cuff can back up fluid and cause a painful swelling condition called lymphedema. Good clinical safety knowledge to keep in mind!

question: Why is modern healthcare now encouraging fathers to get involved during pregnancy?

options.A: Government policies now fine fathers who stay away.
options.B: Women are no longer able to attend clinics alone.
options.C: Shared decision-making improves overall health outcomes.
options.D: Hospitals have extra space to accommodate couples.

explanation: When men are involved, health choices and money are planned together, leading to a healthier family! Keep it up.

question: Why do doctors perform a colposcopy and take a biopsy after a woman gets an abnormal Pap smear result?

options.A: To clean out the entire uterine cavity and prevent future infections
options.B: To examine suspicious areas closely and take a tissue sample for definitive diagnosis
options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels circulating in the pelvic blood vessels
options.D: To instantly cure the viral infection using high-intensity light beams

explanation: Think of a Pap smear as a warning bell, while a colposcopy and biopsy are the detectives that look closer to confirm what is really going on.

question: What is one key reason for conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To allocate scarce health resources where they are needed most
options.B: To increase the patient population inside large urban hospitals
options.C: To eliminate the need for community health workers in rural areas
options.D: To reduce the salaries of local public health administrators

explanation: Exactly! Since resources like funding and medical supplies are often limited, a community diagnosis helps us direct them to the areas that need them most.

question: What is the main use of a yellow, puncture-proof safety box?

options.A: To collect expired liquid syrups and chemical disinfectants safely
options.B: To store office stationery and confidential patient case notes
options.C: To hold organic kitchen food leftovers from the hospital cafeteria
options.D: To safely contain needles and sharps without risk of piercing

explanation: Great job! Safety boxes have hard walls so needles can't poke through and accidentally injure hospital staff.

question: How is an idiosyncratic reaction different from a regular side effect?

options.A: It occurs in only a small number of people regardless of dose
options.B: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose of medicine
options.C: It can be accurately predicted using standard body weight formulas
options.D: It always involves a classic skin rash and itching

explanation: Unlike common side effects that happen to lots of people, idiosyncratic reactions are rare and don't care about the dose size. Great job thinking this through!

question: What is the proper way to position an adult's ear before putting in ear drops?

options.A: Pull the pinna up and back before instilling the drops
options.B: Keep the client sitting upright for thirty minutes after
options.C: Insert the dropper tip firmly deep into the ear canal
options.D: Pull the earlobe straight down before putting in drops

explanation: Correct! Pulling the pinna up and back opens up the canal so the drops slide right down nicely toward the eardrum.

question: Which IV solution is classified as isotonic and commonly used for fluid resuscitation?

options.A: 0.9% Normal Saline
options.B: 5% Dextrose in water
options.C: 3.0% Sodium Chloride
options.D: 0.45% Sodium Chloride

explanation: Normal Saline at 0.9% concentration matches body fluid osmolarity, keeping red blood cells stable while expanding blood volume. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h3)

question: What type of germ causes trichomoniasis?

options.A: Bacterium
options.B: Retrovirus
options.C: Protozoan parasite
options.D: Dermatophyte fungus

explanation: Trichomoniasis is caused by a tiny, swimming parasite known as *Trichomonas vaginalis*.

question: Why is it important to run physical medical tests on someone presenting with severe anxiety symptoms?

options.A: To determine the correct dosage of psychotherapy immediately
options.B: To measure the exact concentration of brain neurotransmitters
options.C: To rule out medical conditions like hyperthyroidism that mimic anxiety
options.D: To prove that the patient is faking psychological distress

explanation: Spot on! Conditions like an overactive thyroid can cause a racing pulse and tremors that look just like anxiety. We always check the physical body first!

question: What triggers the sarcoplasmic reticulum to release a flood of calcium inside a heart cell?

options.A: A small influx of extracellular calcium through membrane channels
options.B: The direct binding of ATP molecules to troponin C
options.C: The sudden drop in intracellular potassium levels
options.D: A massive flood of sodium ions directly from the T-tubules

explanation: It is a chain reaction! A little calcium trickles in from the outside, which triggers a much bigger release of stored calcium inside. Neat, right?

question: What is the first practical step a person should take when starting a weekly meal plan?

options.A: Visiting the local market without a list
options.B: Throwing away all existing canned goods
options.C: Ordering takeout food for the upcoming weekend
options.D: Checking current pantry and refrigerator inventory

explanation: Checking what is already at home prevents buying duplicate items and helps build meals around existing ingredients. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of orienting a newly admitted patient to the ward?

options.A: To give the doctor time to finish other ward rounds
options.B: To test the patient's memory and cognitive function
options.C: To reduce anxiety and help them adjust to the new environment
options.D: To ensure the patient fills out their discharge papers early

explanation: A good orientation helps a frightened or stressed patient feel secure by showing them how things work around the ward. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: A nurse teaches villagers to boil their drinking water to stop cholera. Which part of the disease chain is this targeting?

options.A: The genetic makeup of the host
options.B: The incubation period of the germ
options.C: The vehicle of transmission
options.D: The virulence of the pathogen

explanation: Water acts as the 'vehicle' carrying the germ to people. Boiling it breaks the chain right there. Brilliant public health nursing!

question: Why is fast teamwork among healthcare staff so essential when managing GI complications?

options.A: Conditions can deteriorate into life-threatening emergencies very quickly
options.B: Nurses are not allowed to touch patients without a doctor present
options.C: Medical staff must share paperwork equally among themselves
options.D: Collaborative care guarantees that surgery will never be needed

explanation: You got it! Emergencies like bowel tears or massive bleeding move fast, meaning the team has to act together instantly to keep the patient safe. Teamwork makes the dream work in nursing!

question: What is the easiest and most sensitive way for a nurse to check for early fluid buildup at home?

options.A: Weighing the patient daily at the same time
options.B: Measuring the circumference of the arm
options.C: Asking the patient if they feel thirsty
options.D: Checking shoe size once a week

explanation: Water weighs a lot! A sudden climb on the bathroom scale is almost always the earliest sign that fluid is starting to build up in the body.

question: What is the main job of the intrinsic muscles found completely inside the tongue?

options.A: Supplying blood to the taste buds
options.B: Protruding the tongue out of the mouth
options.C: Changing the overall shape of the tongue
options.D: Anchoring the tongue to the mandible

explanation: Because intrinsic muscles live entirely inside the tongue, they work like a flexible cushion to change its shape when you talk or swallow.

question: What is saliva's main job when you take a bite of food?

options.A: Absorbing simple sugars directly into the bloodstream
options.B: Initiating starch digestion using amylase
options.C: Breaking down complex proteins into amino acids
options.D: Neutralizing stomach acid before swallowing

explanation: Saliva has an enzyme called amylase that immediately starts breaking down starches right inside your mouth. Great job!

question: What happens during the clinical latency stage of HIV?

options.A: The immune system completely eradicates the virus without treatment.
options.B: The virus multiplies slowly and the patient often feels healthy.
options.C: CD4 cell counts rapidly increase above normal levels.
options.D: The patient experiences severe opportunistic infections immediately.

explanation: During this quiet period, the virus stays active but multiplies slowly. Many patients look and feel completely fine, which is why testing is so important!

question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood programs?

options.A: To shorten the duration of pregnancy
options.B: To reduce maternal and neonatal deaths
options.C: To promote exclusive formula feeding
options.D: To completely eliminate normal labor pain

explanation: Spot on! Safe motherhood programs are all about keeping both mothers and newborns safe, healthy, and alive. You've got this!

question: What is the standard temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.A: Minus 20 degrees Celsius to minus 10 degrees Celsius
options.B: Minus 5 degrees Celsius to zero degrees Celsius
options.C: Plus 2 degrees Celsius to plus 8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Plus 15 degrees Celsius to plus 25 degrees Celsius

explanation: Commit +2°C to +8°C to memory! As a nurse managing the cold chain in your clinic, this is your golden rule for keeping vaccines potent.

question: Why does a hospital admission often disrupt a patient's ability to meet basic human needs?

options.A: Hospital environments completely eliminate stress
options.B: Patients no longer care about their personal health
options.C: Familiar daily routines and independence are interrupted
options.D: Healthcare providers automatically handle all needs instantly

explanation: Being in an unfamiliar hospital setting takes away a person's normal independence, making basic tasks harder to manage alone. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following is an example of a three-dimensional instructional aid?

options.A: An audio podcast
options.B: A chalkboard drawing
options.C: A printed textbook page
options.D: Anatomical manikin

explanation: Three-dimensional aids have length, breadth, and thickness, allowing students to touch and examine physical structures like manikins and models. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h3)

question: A nurse wants women to turn up for a new maternal health clinic. What is the best first move with local stakeholders?

options.A: Rely entirely on radio announcements without speaking to community leaders
options.B: Start the clinic secretly to avoid drawing unwanted attention
options.C: Impose strict attendance fines for women who miss antenatal visits
options.D: Involve local chiefs and women leaders early to help design the rollout

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with respected local leaders builds instant trust and makes community members eager to participate.

question: A family caregiver is overwhelmed because their relative with memory loss keeps missing doses and mixing up pill times. What is the most helpful nursing intervention?

options.A: Tell the caregiver to stop giving all medications immediately
options.B: Warn them that missing doses has zero effect on chronic illnesses
options.C: Advise them to let the patient manage everything independently
options.D: Suggest practical tools like a labeled pill organizer and a daily schedule

explanation: Brilliant nursing advice! Simple organizational tools like pill boxes, alarms, and visual charts can lift a huge weight off family caregivers and keep patients safe on their medication routine.

question: Which food texture is safest for a patient with severe swallowing difficulties and missing teeth?

options.A: Regular solid
options.B: Raw vegetables
options.C: Pureed
options.D: Mechanically soft

explanation: Pureed foods are smooth and need zero chewing effort, making them much safer and easier for a struggling patient to swallow.

question: A patient with advanced lung cancer takes chemotherapy to shrink a tumor and also takes medicine for breathlessness and pain. What type of care is this?

options.A: Purely experimental care with no proven benefit
options.B: Curative care only, because pain is a minor symptom
options.C: A combination of curative and palliative care
options.D: Palliative care only, because chemotherapy has stopped

explanation: This is a great combo! The chemo fights the cancer (curative), while the pain meds keep the patient comfortable (palliative). They work wonderfully together.

question: What is a key prevention message nurses should teach families to stop Lassa fever at home?

options.A: Keep doors and windows wide open during the evening hours
options.B: Dry all harvested grains directly on bare soil surfaces
options.C: Store food items in tightly sealed, rodent-proof containers
options.D: Keep pet cats away from all residential cooking areas

explanation: Locking up food in secure containers keeps rats away and stops them from contaminating your grains with urine and faeces.

question: Which preparation is specifically designed as a liquid instillation into the rectum?

options.A: Transdermal patch
options.B: Enema
options.C: Sublingual tablet
options.D: Suppository

question: Which of these should normally NOT slip through the kidney's filter into your urine?

options.A: Sodium mineral ions
options.B: Filtered water molecules
options.C: Large plasma proteins
options.D: Dissolved glucose molecules

explanation: Correct! A healthy kidney filter has tiny pores that keep big things like proteins and blood cells safely inside your bloodstream.

question: What type of clothing is best for someone working outdoors in areas with lots of stinging insects?

options.A: Brightly colored floral shirts that blend with nature
options.B: Shorts and sleeveless tops to stay cool in the heat
options.C: Light-colored, long-sleeved clothing that fits smoothly
options.D: Dark wool garments to absorb sweat effectively

explanation: You got it! Smooth, light-covered, long clothes protect your skin and help you avoid attracting insects that love dark colors and floral patterns.

question: What is the primary function of carbohydrates in the human body?

options.A: Providing primary energy for daily activities
options.B: Producing essential hormones for growth
options.C: Regulating body temperature through sweating
options.D: Repairing damaged muscle tissues and organs

explanation: Carbohydrates are broken down into glucose, which serves as the body's main and most efficient energy source. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T015#GNS227_U4_T015_h1)

question: How can a nurse show gender-transformative practice during a community health talk?

options.A: Telling male participants that health matters are not relevant to them
options.B: Encouraging both fathers and mothers to share responsibility for child nutrition
options.C: Focusing exclusively on traditional remedies endorsed by elders
options.D: Instructing only women to attend because childcare is solely a female duty

explanation: Spot on! Involving both parents in childcare and nutrition breaks down rigid stereotypes and leads to healthier families.

question: A patient takes daily medication that successfully controls their high blood pressure. However, they feel drained, skip workouts, and eat junk food. Where do they fit on the wellness scale?

options.A: Completely outside the continuum because they take medication
options.B: At the far left end experiencing premature death
options.C: In the neutral point, free of disease symptoms but below optimal wellness
options.D: At the far right end representing high-level wellness

explanation: Spot on! Keeping symptoms under control puts them in the safe middle zone. True wellness takes a bit more active care with lifestyle habits.

question: Why do specialty nurses, like nurse anesthetists, pay higher malpractice insurance rates?

options.A: They are legally required to own three separate insurance policies at the same time
options.B: Hospital administrators force specialty nurses to subsidize general floor coverage
options.C: Insurance companies charge extra fees for nurses who work night shifts

explanation: Higher risk areas deal with critical life-and-death procedures where a small mistake can have massive consequences, so insurance costs more.

question: Why is hypertension frequently called the 'silent killer'?

options.A: It usually causes no symptoms in its early stages
options.B: Patients refuse to talk about their diagnosis
options.C: It stops the heart without any warning sounds
options.D: It only affects people who are sleeping

explanation: Because high blood pressure rarely causes physical discomfort initially, individuals often remain unaware of their condition until complications arise. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h3)

question: Which family planning supply method gives dual protection against BOTH pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Male condoms
options.B: Oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal creams
options.D: Cervical caps

explanation: Condoms act as a physical shield that blocks body fluids, stopping both conception and many infections at once. Smart nursing knowledge!

question: Which of the following is a common physical complication of performing high-quality chest compressions?

options.A: Severe internal bleeding
options.B: Rupture of the liver
options.C: Puncture of both lungs
options.D: Rib or sternal fractures

question: What is the primary purpose of the cold chain in immunization programs?

options.A: To speed up the delivery of medical supplies to large cities
options.B: To keep vaccines within safe temperature ranges so they remain potent
options.C: To store expired medications safely away from patients
options.D: To freeze liquid vaccines completely solid before use

explanation: The cold chain protects heat-sensitive vaccines from losing their medical effectiveness before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T71#GNS214_U1_T71_h4)

question: Why do joint sprains (injured ligaments) usually take a really long time to heal?

options.A: Muscles pull the torn ends apart constantly
options.B: Synovial fluid continuously dissolves new scar tissue
options.C: Fibrocartilage replaces all normal collagen
options.D: Ligaments have a poor blood supply

question: If your goal is to learn proper aseptic technique for surgery, which activity best helps you achieve it?

options.A: Listening to an audio podcast about common surgical instruments

options.C: Writing a three-page essay on the history of hospital hygiene

explanation: To learn a physical skill, you've got to practice it hands-on in the lab! Theory is important, but action makes it stick.

question: Which government sector is mainly responsible for teaching health habits and running school hygiene programs?

options.A: Agriculture
options.B: Finance

options.D: Public Works

question: What are the two main categories of hormone disorders?

options.A: Benign or malignant

options.D: Excess or deficiency

explanation: Keep it simple: hormone problems usually happen because the body makes either too much (excess) or too little (deficiency) of a hormone.

question: Why does lacking thiamine cause brain cells to die so quickly?

options.A: It disrupts critical energy pathways and glucose metabolism in neurons
options.B: It causes massive bacterial infections inside the cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: It triggers an autoimmune attack directly targeting the myelin sheath
options.D: It increases intracranial pressure by blocking the reabsorption of CSF

explanation: Think of thiamine as the spark plug for brain cells to burn glucose. Without it, the cells literally starve for energy and shut down.

question: How do digital charts in an EMR help nurses keep an eye on vital signs?

options.A: By automatically discharging the patient when vitals normalize
options.B: By making it easier to spot trends and early signs of patient worsening
options.C: By replacing the need to manually measure blood pressure or pulse
options.D: By sending text messages directly to the patient's family members

explanation: Graphical charts lay out numbers over time so you can spot little changes before they turn into major emergencies. You've got this!

question: What common physical thing inside the rectum can block a drug from working well?

question: Who are the key community gatekeepers a nurse should involve to help change harmful food taboos?

options.A: Foreign tourists visiting the local village market
options.B: Commercial transport drivers operating local buses
options.C: Traditional rulers, religious leaders, and elder matriarchs

question: Why is it dangerous to stop taking a beta-blocker all of a sudden?

options.C: It permanently damages the smooth muscle lining of peripheral arteries

question: A patient asks if she should use commercial feminine hygiene sprays and douches to keep her vulva clean. What is the best nursing response?

options.B: Switch to a strongly scented soap instead of a spray.

explanation: Commercial sprays and douches often do more harm than good by washing away healthy protective flora and introducing irritating perfumes. You're learning how to give safe, evidence-based advice!

question: Why do our hands and fingers take up such a huge chunk of space on the motor homunculus?

options.A: They require intricate, precise, and complex motor control
options.B: They have a much larger physical mass than the legs
options.C: They are closer to the brain than the lower extremities

question: What is one of the biggest duties of a community health nurse when dealing with NCDs?

options.A: Manufacturing affordable insulin and blood pressure drugs in local clinics
options.B: Performing major neurosurgeries in rural primary health centers
options.C: Bridging the gap between formal health facilities and grassroots populations
options.D: Enforcing strict national prison sentences for people who eat junk food

explanation: Spot on! Community nurses take health education, screenings, and support right to the doorsteps and neighborhoods where people live.

question: Why is it actually a good thing that the mother's blood and the baby's blood do not mix directly?

options.A: To keep the fetal body temperature lower than the mother's core temperature
options.B: To allow the placenta to produce hormones without interference
options.C: To prevent the mother's high blood pressure from damaging fragile fetal blood vessels
options.D: To stop the fetus from rejecting the mother's blood cells immediately

explanation: Spot on! Mother's blood pressure can be quite high, so keeping the bloodstreams separate protects the baby's tiny, delicate blood vessels from bursting.

question: What is the main reason for using an incinerator to burn pathological waste?

options.A: To reduce organic materials completely into sterile ash
options.B: To filter chemical fumes out of the hospital laundry
options.C: To cool down heavy laboratory equipment safely
options.D: To melt plastic containers into reusable water bottles

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to learning in a hospital setting?

options.A: Constant noise and staff interruptions on the ward
options.B: High levels of physical pain and anxiety
options.C: Quiet, distraction-free private recovery rooms
options.D: Language differences between nurse and patient

question: What happens when a patient's kidney function suddenly drops, affecting drug clearance?

options.C: Drug excretion stops completely within a few minutes.

question: A 12-year-old child is brought to the clinic for repeatedly skipping school and running away. How should you as a nurse classify these actions?

options.A: Adult felonies
options.B: Violent offenses
options.C: Property offenses
options.D: Status offenses

question: What do we mean by the 'triple dividend' of investing in adolescent health?

options.A: It provides three free medications for every patient visit

options.C: It requires three separate doctors to examine every teenager
options.D: It triples hospital revenue over three financial years

question: Which bacteria is most commonly linked to undercooked poultry and eggs?

question: Which muscle site is generally considered the safest and most recommended for adult IM injections?

options.D: Vastus lateralis

question: A nurse wears gloves and a face shield while cleaning a bloody wound on a patient with an unknown diagnosis. What is the nurse practicing?

options.A: Active surveillance
options.B: Tertiary prevention

question: Why are predictive equations used in hospital wards instead of direct calorimetry?

options.C: Calorimetry chambers are required by law

question: Why do adult males typically have a higher resting metabolic rate than females of the same size?

options.A: Their digestive tract is physically longer

question: A patient has minor bruises and seems too terrified to speak, while her partner answers every question for her. What should you suspect as a nurse?

options.B: A pattern of controlling intimate partner violence
options.C: Normal communication patterns in a healthy marriage

question: What is the main lab test used to find parasite eggs in clinic patients?

question: What happens to a hospital's safety culture when management ignores staff reports and refuses to fix staff shortages?

options.A: Nurses become more efficient and independent
options.B: The safety culture erodes and trust breaks down
options.C: Staff morale improves and errors decrease
options.D: Patient satisfaction scores increase rapidly

question: If a patient shows clear signs of shock after eating an allergen, which classic symptom might actually be completely missing?

options.A: Severe stomach cramps
options.B: Swelling of the tongue
options.C: Hives or skin rashes
options.D: Difficulty breathing

question: Which category of healthcare waste includes discarded scalpels and broken glass ampoules?

question: A nurse sets up a desk in the village square to check blood sugar levels for healthy adults. What level of prevention is this?

options.B: Primary prevention

options.D: Secondary prevention

question: Why is metoclopramide a big NO-GO for a patient with a confirmed bowel blockage (obstruction)?

question: Why do pharmaceutical companies often need special incentives to develop orphan drugs?

question: Which patient is the best fit for a subacute care unit?
